topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: Answer the following about the political career of Franklin D. Roosevelt.
question.text: In 1932, FDR defeated this man to become president. This president's administration oversaw the beginning of the Great Depression, for which he was widely unpopular.
question.clue: Near the end of his term, he sent Douglas MacArthur to clear out the Bonus Army that was protesting for relief from the Great Depression.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the namesakes of airports around the world.
swap.text: This former New York City mayor is the namesake of an airport which Joe Biden compared to a "third world country".
swap.answerHtml: Fiorello La Guardia [or Fiorello Henry La Guardia or Fiorello Enrico La Guardia]
swap.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

question.leadin: Name some organizations established during the New Deal.
question.text: This largest New Deal agency was created by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and provided jobs and income to the unemployed; it also operated large arts, media, and literacy projects.
question.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

swap.text: During the "mobster" era, the FBI received help from the infamous "lady in red" to corner and kill this "Public Enemy No.1," in Chicago.
swap.clue: This leader of the Terror Gang had such confederates as George "Baby Face" Nelson.

question.text: During this "dark day," the value of the Dow Jones fell some 12% as investors received margin calls and flooded the markets with cheap stocks. It would mark the end of the Roaring Twenties and usher in the Great Depression.

swap.leadin: Douglas MacArthur used army infantry to help the police disperse this group.
swap.text: Identify this group of army veterans which marched on Washington in 1932 to demand redemption of their service certificates from World War I.
swap.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

question.leadin: Name some things about colorful dogs in American history.
question.text: Yellow-dog contracts were banned by this 1932 law. This law was sponsored by a Nebraska Senator who founded the Tennessee Valley Authority and a future New York City mayor who now names an airport in Queens.
question.clue: The ruling in New Negro Alliance v. Sanitary Grocery Company applied this act to say federal courts could not prevent picketing.

swap.leadin: Name these things about U.S. foreign policy.
swap.text: To emphasize cooperation and trade rather than military force in Central and South America, FDR established this policy in his 1933 inaugural address.
swap.clue: This policy during the FDR administration in which the U.S. attempted to mend its relations with Latin America. Instead of interfering in other countries' affairs, the U.S. would act like the namesake of this policy.

question.text: The author of Change, Hope, and the Bomb, David Eli Llienthal, served as its chairman for five years. For 15 points, name this New Deal agency which brought electric power to the rural Southeast.
question.clue: The Muscle Shoals Bill, vetoed by Herbert Hoover, was the initial impetus for this organization.

swap.text: As Vice President, Wallace argued with Jesse Jones, the extremely powerful head of this institution founded during the Hoover term to provide loans to banks and businesses.
swap.clue: This entity, at one point led by Jesse Jones, was created by the Hoover administration to hand out money to the states during the Great Depression.

question.text: This physician developed a plan for state-funded old-age pensions as a way to stimulate economic spending during the Depression. While FDR eventually adopted the Social Security Act, this man was not pleased with the conservative changes the President made to his proposal.
question.clue: This doctor, another critic of FDR's New Deal, popularized a namesake national pension plan which influenced the Social Security Act.

swap.leadin: This man was the Chairman of the State Factory Investigating Committee after the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire.
swap.text: Name this New York Senator who is best known for being the namesake of the 1935 National Labor Relations Act, which created the National Labor Relations Board and guaranteed the right of workers to form unions.

question.text: Franklin Roosevelt undertook a program of lowering tariffs through this first secretary of state. He engineered the passage of the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act and formulated the Good Neighbor Policy.
question.clue: This longest-serving Secretary of State ran unsuccessfully for President in 1928 before serving Franklin Delano Roosevelt and later won the Nobel Peace Prize for "co-initiating the United Nations".

swap.leadin: During a visit to China, this man was infatuated by Soong Mei-Ling and may have had an affair with her.
swap.text: Name this man who, as a representative for the utility corporation C&S, spent 7 years arguing against the TVA. This man unsuccessfully ran for president against FDR in 1940.
swap.clue: This lawyer and corporate president of Commonwealth and Southern Corporation who was the Republican candidate for President in 1940.

question.leadin: When asked to head this agency, Hugh Johnson bizarrely declared "It will be red fire at first and dead cats afterward."
question.text: Name this New Deal agency that asked employers to sign the Presidential Reemployment Agreement, an industrial code designed to maintain wages and limit production, as part of his "Blue Eagle" campaign.
question.clue: The business community soured on the 1933 law creating this agency, which was directed by Hugh Samuel Johnson and symbolized with a blue eagle. The "sick chicken" case, Schechter v. US, eliminated it.

swap.text: Amended by the Landrum-Griffin act, this New Deal legislation created the National Labor Relations Board and allowed for collective bargaining, catalyzing the growth of labor unions.
swap.clue: It was called unconstitutional by the American Liberty League and, in a Supreme Court case, Jones and Laughlin Steel claimed that it was not consistent with the commerce clause, but Chief Justice Hughes sided with the government.

question.text: This notorious section of the Glass-Steagall Act prohibited banks from paying interest on checking accounts and was repealed as part of the 1986 reform.
question.clue: This portion of the Glass-Steagall Act set maximum interest rates on demand deposits. Though mostly phased out in the 1980s, it still prohibits the earning of any interest from a commercial checking account.

swap.text: This Mayor of New York City from 1926 to 1932 publicized his visit to Tom Mooney while Mooney was in jail. His marriage to the Ziegfield showgirl Betty Compton gained him the nickname "Gentleman."
swap.answerHtml: Jimmy Walker [or James John Walker; or James J. Walker]

question.text: This FDR advisor ran the Works Progress Administration. Before American entrance into World War II, he coordinated unofficial negotiations with Winston Churchill.
question.clue: This supervisor of the WPA was one of Roosevelt's closest advisors and served as Secretary of Commerce for Roosevelt near the end of his second term. He served as FDR's primary emissary to Britain during WWII and oversaw the lend lease program.

swap.text: The effectiveness of the RFC was somewhat compromised by the requirement that it publish the names of the banks receiving loans, which was forced by this Speaker of the House and later Vice President. His nickname referred to his endorsement of the cactus as a state flower.
swap.clue: For a time, the so-called "Board of Education" was known as his "Dog House" because of his ability to forcibly persuade fellow Congressmen.
